justification: Decides which reviewed rows become live provisions. Ten chapters could not commit at all — every one died on uq_provisions_current_identity and rolled back — because approved rows accumulate across repeated reviews of an unchanged PDF and all of them were inserted. That held 101 controls citing documents they were not read from, and DQ-70 is the only blocker on OC-10.

pre_impl.existing_data: dcp_review_queue (council, chapter_key, status, ref_number, document_id, new_text, new_page, change_type, id) and the unique index uq_provisions_current_identity on regulatory_provisions, read from pg_indexes rather than assumed. No schema change, no new query — one existing SELECT gains a DISTINCT ON.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The commit assumed the approved rows for a chapter describe one version of it. They do not: a chapter re-read three times with its PDF unchanged carries three complete approved batches, all with the same source_content_hash. Measured — hornsby/part-1-general 24 + 26 + 27 across 28 July, 2 September and 18 September.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Applies to every future commit. Changes no stored row by itself; it changes which rows a commit inserts. The older approved rows are left to the cleanup that already follows a successful commit.
pre_impl.external_source_error: None — no network, no document is read here. The council's PDF was parsed long before this point.
pre_impl.frontend_type: No API or component change: this runs in the commit worker, and the review UI reads the queue rather than this path.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Two directions. Too broad and a stale July text overwrites September's — prevented by ordering id DESC, which a test pins explicitly. Too narrow and a genuine amendment never lands — prevented because the dedupe is per ref_number, so every distinct provision still commits. The separate currency guard (approved rows spanning more than one source hash) is untouched and pinned by test, because that one catches a different failure: the PDF changing after review rather than being read twice.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: The insert-site fetch loses DISTINCT ON (ref_number); the ordering flips to id ASC (which would resurrect an older review over a newer one); the select list stops matching the five columns the insert loop unpacks positionally; or the multi-hash currency guard is removed.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Both halves of the defect were planted in the source and CAUGHT: reverting the dedupe, and keeping the oldest row instead of the newest. 4 passed here and 9 passed in the existing commit-worker suites. Verified against production, not only in tests: before the fix the commit run reported 12 committed / 11 failed with ten of those failures reading 'duplicate key value violates unique constraint uq_provisions_current_identity'; after it, 10 committed / 1 failed, 'nothing went backwards', and DQ-70 fell 177 -> 151. The single remaining failure is the section-loss guard refusing a chapter whose headings degraded because its OCR fetch timed out — a different and correct refusal.

functions.name: commit_chapter
functions.file_line: scripts/dcp_commit_approved.py — the insert-site fetch inside it
functions.input: A council and chapter_key whose approved rows have already passed the blocking, currency and section-loss guards.
functions.output: The latest approved row per ref_number, in ref_number order, each inserted as a provision. Previously every approved row for the chapter, oldest first, which inserted the same provision two or three times.
functions.if_none: A chapter with no approved rows yields no rows and inserts nothing; the caller's counters treat that as zero inserted rather than as success.

values.name: ORDER BY ref_number, id DESC
values.value: id DESC — the newest review of each provision wins
values.why: Ascending would take the oldest, so a July text would overwrite the September one that was actually reviewed against the current document. The direction is the whole correctness of the fix, which is why a test asserts DESC by name rather than just asserting a DISTINCT ON is present.
values.source: Measured 2026-09-19 on hornsby, blacktown and georges_river, each holding three dated batches at one source hash.
values.if_missing: Without the ordering clause DISTINCT ON picks an arbitrary row, so the committed text would vary between runs of the same data — the worst version of this bug, because it would look fixed.
values.read_at: scripts/dcp_commit_approved.py — the SELECT feeding the insert loop.

queries.purpose: Fetch the reviewed rows to insert as live provisions for one chapter, taking only the most recent decision for each provision.
queries.where_clause: council = %s AND chapter_key = %s AND status = 'approved', with DISTINCT ON (ref_number) and ORDER BY ref_number, id DESC. Scoped to one chapter per call; the surrounding transaction rolls back the whole chapter on any error.

break_it.scenario: An older approved review overwrites a newer one.
break_it.what_happens: A provision reverts to text reviewed against an earlier reading, silently, and the chapter still reports as committed.
break_it.how: id DESC, asserted by name in a test. Planting id ASC is caught.

break_it.scenario: The dedupe hides a genuine second provision that happens to share a ref_number.
break_it.what_happens: A genuine clause would never reach the live provisions, and nothing would report its absence.
break_it.how: ref_number is the provision's identity in this pipeline — it is what the unique index keys on alongside document_id and section_header, and what the queue's own removal and change rows are matched by. Two live provisions under one ref_number are not representable downstream.
break_it.repro: SELECT ref_number, count(*) FROM regulatory_provisions WHERE is_current GROUP BY 1 HAVING count(*) > 1 — the identity the index already enforces.

break_it.scenario: The currency guard is dropped because this fix looks like it supersedes it.
break_it.what_happens: A stale approval — reviewed against a PDF that has since changed — commits silently.
break_it.how: A test asserts the hash_variants > 1 skip is still present. The two guards catch different things: that one a changed document, this one a document read twice.

break_it.scenario: Old approved rows keep accumulating for chapters that never commit.
break_it.what_happens: The queue grows and every future run re-reads rows that were decided months ago.
break_it.how: Not addressed here. The cleanup runs only after a successful commit, so a chapter blocked for another reason keeps its history. It is now harmless to the commit, but it is still there.
break_it.repro: SELECT council, chapter_key, created_at::date, count(*) FROM dcp_review_queue WHERE status='approved' GROUP BY 1,2,3

break_it.scenario: A chapter still refuses to commit after this fix, for an unrelated reason.
break_it.what_happens: It looks like the fix did not work.
break_it.how: Expected: ku_ring_gai/section-a-part-4-1-secondary-dwellings still refuses, on the section-loss guard, because its re-read lost every heading when the OCR fetch timed out and fell back to config section names. That is a different defect and the guard is right to hold it.
break_it.repro: python scripts/dcp_commit_approved.py --commit — the refusal names the chapter and its lost sections.

post_merge.db_reset: No. The fix changes which rows a commit inserts; it rewrites nothing that is already live, and the run it enabled reported 'nothing went backwards'.
post_merge.manual_verify: No — already verified against production: 10 chapters committed that could not commit before, and DQ-70 fell from 177 to 151.
